title: What if the moon suddenly disappeared tonight?
formula: Strange act (you carry a lawn chair DOWN to the sea while 4,000 people run UP the hill) -> why (the moon blinked out, every phone says giant wave) -> goal (you won't leave Grandma's snack shack) -> rival's perfect version (Brad: 500 sandbags, floodlights, a live stream) mocks you; doubter (Mia: 'We're gonna drown') -> weird prep chain (a stick at the waterline, every light off, popcorn) -> setback (the sea pulls back, Brad: tsunami!) -> tension stretch (ten steps, twenty, thirty) -> explain mid-danger (bedsheet analogy) -> undercut (just a boring tide) -> stick pays off (tides a third) -> reversal (no moon = darkest nights: Brad's floodlights pull every moth, your dark beach gets the stars, popcorn pays off) -> loop: 4,000 people bring a lawn chair
loop: Line 1: you carry a lawn chair down to the sea while 4,000 people run up the hill. Last: the next night, all 4,000 people bring a lawn chair (down to your beach).
facts: Without the moon only the sun raises tides; its tidal pull is ~46% of the moon's, leaving roughly a third of today's tidal range (ScienceABC, Astronoo; ZME Science says 50-75% lower). Script: 'stops a third of the way'.

No giant wave: the moon's tidal bulge would settle like an ordinary ebb over hours, not surge (Live Science / Space.com 'what if the moon disappeared'; forum physics agrees). The bedsheet analogy is ours.
The sea pulling back from the shore is a real tsunami warning sign (Brad's line is a true fact misapplied).

Full moon ~0.25 lux vs clear moonless night with starlight + airglow ~0.002 lux: ~125x (Wikipedia 'Daylight' / 'Orders of magnitude (illuminance)'). Script: 'a hundred times darker' (vs a full-moon night).
Moonlight washes out faint stars; dark moonless skies show far more stars and the Milky Way (real). 'Exploding with stars' is comic exaggeration.
Light traps catch more insects on dark (new-moon) nights; 'every moth for fifty miles finds Brad' is comic exaggeration.
4,000 people, 500 sandbags, 50 miles: story numbers, not fact claims.

lines.narration: You carry a lawn chair down to the ocean, while 4,000 people run up the *hill*.
lines.spoken: You carry a lawn chair DOWN to the ocean, while four thousand people run up the hill.
lines.scene: Cold open, night beach town: you walk down the beach path with a folding lawn chair under your arm, against a stream of townsfolk with flashlights, suitcases, a fish tank, a grandpa carrying a TV, all running uphill.
lines.camera: Low wide on the path, you walking toward the lens against the crowd; hard cut on '4,000' to a high wide of the hill road, a river of flashlights
lines.gag: You are the only one walking the other way; somebody runs past carrying a whole fridge

lines.narration: Because ten minutes ago, the moon just... *blinked* out.
lines.spoken: Because ten minutes ago, the moon just... blinked out.
lines.scene: Flash back ten minutes: the full moon over the bay, a dog on the pier howling at it. The moon switches off like a light bulb, leaving a moon-shaped patch of black sky.
lines.camera: Tilt up from the howling dog to the moon; hold on the black hole in the sky
lines.gag: The moon goes out with a light-switch click; the dog stops mid-howl and looks at the camera

lines.narration: And every phone in town says the same thing: giant *wave*.
lines.spoken: And every phone in town says the same thing: giant wave.
lines.scene: Back on the hill road: dozens of phone screens light the running faces, each showing the same alert: a huge cartoon wave and 'NO MOON = MEGA WAVE?!'.
lines.camera: Fast push across a row of phone screens
lines.gag: Every phone shows the same alert at the same moment, glowing on 30 terrified faces

lines.narration: But you're not leaving Grandma's snack *shack*.
lines.scene: The beach: a tiny wooden snack shack, sign 'SHELLY'S SNACKS', a giant fibreglass hot dog on the roof, Grandma's framed photo by the hatch. You unfold the chair in front of it and sit, arms crossed.
lines.camera: Low push-in on you in the chair, the shack behind
lines.gag: You snap the chair open with one flick and sit like a king guarding a castle made of hot dogs

lines.narration: Up on the hill, Brad the realtor has 500 sandbags, floodlights, and a *live stream*.
lines.spoken: Up on the hill, Brad the realtor has five hundred sandbags, floodlights, and a live stream.
lines.scene: Brad's hilltop fortress: a pyramid of sandbags round his big house, two blazing floodlights, Brad in a pastel suit and a bike helmet on top, phone on a selfie stick, a screen behind him: 'LIVE 12K'.
lines.camera: Telephoto from the beach up to Brad, crane up the sandbag pyramid
lines.gag: Brad poses on the sandbags like a mountaineer on a summit, selfie stick raised like a flag

lines.narration: "Enjoy the wave, chair *guy*!"
lines.speaker: brad
lines.scene: Brad points down at you for the stream; his comment feed scrolls with laughing emojis.
lines.camera: Telephoto MCU of Brad laughing, hard cut
lines.gag: Brad's face fills his own phone screen, the laughing emojis rain down it

lines.narration: Even your little sister Mia thinks you've *lost* it.
lines.scene: Mia (9, two puffy pigtails, yellow raincoat, a goldfish in a bag) tugs your sleeve, the goldfish staring too.
lines.camera: Two-shot, you in the chair, Mia leaning in
lines.gag: Mia and her goldfish make the exact same worried face

lines.narration: "We're gonna *drown*."
lines.speaker: mia
lines.scene: Mia CU, eyes huge.
lines.camera: Hard cut to Mia close
lines.gag: The goldfish in her bag nods

lines.narration: You don't answer. You push a stick into the sand, right at the *water*.
lines.scene: You walk to the waterline and push a long stick upright into the wet sand, right where the foam stops.
lines.camera: Macro insert: the stick sinking into the sand as foam washes round it
lines.gag: You plant it with a little twist, like a flag on the moon

lines.narration: Then you switch off every light in the *shack*.
lines.scene: Inside the shack: the fridge glow, the neon HOT DOGS sign, the string lights; you flick them off one by one until it's dark.
lines.camera: Inside the hatch, hard cuts on each switch
lines.gag: The neon hot dog fizzles out last, sadly drooping

lines.narration: And you make *popcorn*.
lines.scene: A pan of popcorn pops on the camping stove; you pour it into a huge bucket and sit back down in the chair.
lines.camera: Macro on the popping pan, cut to you in the chair with the bucket
lines.gag: A kernel pops straight into your open mouth

lines.narration: Then the ocean starts pulling *back*.
lines.scene: The foam slides away from the stick, the waterline sliding back down the beach, wet sand gleaming.
lines.camera: Low over the sand, pulling back with the water
lines.gag: A crab on the sand sprints after the water

lines.narration: "It pulls back before a *tsunami*!"
lines.speaker: brad
lines.scene: Brad on the sandbags, screaming at his phone; the town behind him screams too.
lines.camera: Telephoto CU of Brad, impact shake
lines.gag: Brad's helmet pops up off his head

lines.narration: Ten steps. Twenty. Thirty. Your stick stands in dry *sand*.
lines.spoken: Ten steps. Twenty. THIRTY. Your stick stands in dry sand.
lines.scene: The water keeps sliding away from the stick; Mia grabs your arm with both hands; you don't move.
lines.camera: Three hard cuts, each wider: the gap between stick and water grows; end on you, popcorn bucket still in your lap
lines.gag: Mia hides behind the popcorn bucket

lines.narration: You see, the moon pulled the ocean up in a bump, like a hand lifting a *bedsheet*.
lines.scene: Analogy mini-set: a bed in a cosy bedroom; a giant hand (moon-white) pinches the middle of the blue bedsheet and lifts it into a hump.
lines.camera: Dissolve in; push in on the hump
lines.gag: A tiny toy boat rides on top of the bedsheet hump

lines.narration: Let go, and the sheet doesn't *slam*. It just... settles.
lines.scene: The hand vanishes; the sheet slowly sinks flat, the toy boat gently lowering with it. Match cut to the ocean, flat and calm.
lines.camera: Slow tilt down with the sheet, match cut to the bay
lines.gag: The toy boat lands without spilling a drop

lines.narration: The water stops. No wave. Just a slow, boring *tide*.
lines.scene: The bay lies flat and calm; a single tiny wave lops onto the sand.
lines.camera: Wide hold on the calm bay, you and Mia small in the foreground
lines.gag: The tiniest wave in history flops onto the beach

lines.narration: And when it comes back, it stops a third of the way to your *stick*. Now only the sun is *pulling*.
lines.scene: Hours later: the tide creeps back in and stops far short of the stick; a line of dark wet sand marks a third of the way.
lines.camera: Low along the sand from the stick to the stopped waterline
lines.gag: The foam reaches toward the stick and gives up, like it's out of breath

lines.narration: But the moon was also the world's biggest nightlight. Without it, nights get a hundred times *darker*.
lines.scene: Wide of the whole bay: the town goes inky black, only Brad's floodlights blazing on the hill.
lines.camera: Fast pull-out to the widest shot of the video
lines.gag: Brad's hill is the only lit thing in the whole world, like a birthday cake in a dark room

lines.narration: So Brad's floodlights are the brightest thing for fifty miles, and every moth for fifty miles finds *Brad*.
lines.spoken: So Brad's floodlights are the brightest thing for fifty miles, and every moth for fifty miles finds BRAD.
lines.scene: A huge cloud of moths swirls into Brad's floodlights and over Brad; his stream shows only moths.
lines.camera: Telephoto push on Brad disappearing into moths
lines.gag: Brad's live stream screen is 100 % moth

lines.narration: Down on your dark beach, Mia looks up, and the sky is *exploding* with stars.
lines.scene: Mia and you in the chair, faces lit faintly blue; overhead the Milky Way blazes across the sky. You pass her the popcorn.
lines.camera: Low angle tilt up from your faces to the star-packed sky
lines.gag: Mia's mouth drops open so wide a popcorn kernel falls in; her goldfish looks up too

lines.narration: The next night, 4,000 people bring a lawn *chair*.
lines.spoken: The next night, four thousand people bring a lawn chair.
lines.scene: Next night: the beach packed edge to edge with lawn chairs under the stars, the shack hatch open and selling popcorn; end on your smug face in close-up, chairs blurred behind.
lines.camera: Mirror of the opening low wide (now everyone walks DOWN with chairs), then a CU of your smug face
lines.gag: A sea of lawn chairs; a moth-covered Brad sneaks in carrying one too
